content: Excessive stress can disrupt the structural development of the brain during its formative years, as highlighted in Working Paper No. 3 by the National Scientific Council on the Developing Child at Harvard University in 2005. Oberklaid and Efron (2005) discussed the identification and management of developmental delays in their article published in Australian Family Physician (Vol. 34, Issue 9, pp. 739–742). Palfrey and colleagues conducted a 25-year follow-up study on the Brookline Early Education Project, with findings published in Pediatrics (2005, Vol. 116, Issue 1, pp. 144–152). Patel et al. (2004) examined the impact of maternal mental health on infant growth in low-income countries, presenting new evidence from South Asia in the British Medical Journal (Vol. 328, pp. 820–823). Pelto and colleagues (2000) emphasized the critical link between interventions for physical growth and psychological development in a report by the World Health Organization's Department of Child and Adolescent Health and Development in Geneva, Switzerland. Rahman (2007) explored the challenges and opportunities in developing psychological interventions for perinatal depression in rural Pakistan through a multi-method study published in the Archives of Women's Mental Health (Vol. 10, pp. 211–219). In a related study, Rahman, Roberts, and Husain (2009) conducted a cluster-randomized trial of a parent-based intervention to support early infant development in low-income countries, with results published in Child: Care, Health and Development (Vol. 35, pp. 56–62). Richter (2004) underscored the importance of caregiver-child interactions for the survival and healthy development of young children in a report by the World Health Organization's Department of Child and Adolescent Health. Additionally, Richter, Foster, and Sherr (2006) addressed the psychosocial needs of young children in the context of HIV/AIDS in their publication, Where the Heart Is, by the Bernard van Leer Foundation in The Hague, Netherlands. Richter (2000) also presented on child development interventions in an invited seminar for the World Health Organization Seminar Series. Squires, Bricker, and LaWanda (1997) revised the parent-completed developmental screening tool, the Ages and Stages Questionnaires, as detailed in the Journal of Pediatric Psychology (Vol. 22, Issue 3, pp. 313–328). Shonkoff and Phillips (2000) provided a comprehensive exploration of early childhood development in their book, From Neurons to Neighborhoods: The Science of Early Childhood Development, published by the National Academy Press in Washington, DC. Vygotsky (1978) contributed foundational insights into the development of higher psychological processes in his work, Mind in Society, published by Harvard University Press. Finally, Walker et al. (2007) identified risk factors for adverse child development outcomes in developing countries in their article published in The Lancet (Vol. 369, pp. 145–157).
